- Stems are **bright green and moist** while pods are **fully mature (tan/brown, dry)**
- No leaf symptoms visible — leaves have already senesced
- Plants appear to be at harvest maturity stage but stems refuse to senesce
- Surrounding plant material is dead/brown

This matches **Green_stem_disorder** (green stems persisting while pods mature) or **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus** (also causes green stems after pod maturity). Let me check reference images.

The Green_stem_disorder reference is a **near-identical match** — green moist stems with mature tan/brown pods, dark soil background, no leaf tissue remaining. The top-right and bottom-left panels of the reference match the test image almost exactly.

Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus shows leaf mottling and insect vectors — completely different appearance.

One more check for confirmation:

Soybean Dwarf Mosaic Virus shows green, lush, leafy plants with yellowing — completely different from the test image showing bare green stems with mature pods.

**Conclusion:** The test image is a textbook Green_stem_disorder case — stems remain bright green and moist while pods are fully matured and tan/brown, with no leaf tissue remaining. The visual match to the reference collage is excellent.
